# Wheel Reinvention Index

<!-- Generated by scripts/wheel-index.js. Do not edit by hand; run `npm run index` to regenerate. -->

_As of 2026-07-12._

## Methodology

The Wheel Reinvention Index measures how often a language model reinvents the wheel — reaches for a hand-rolled or freshly-installed solution when a lower rung on the [reuse ladder](../src/core/ladder.js) already covers the need. Each model runs the [behavior cases](../benchmarks/behavior-cases.json) twice: once **baseline** (no Prior Art gate) and once **gate-enabled**. For every case we score whether the model landed on the expected reuse rung.

**Reinvention rate** is the fraction of cases where the *baseline* (un-gated) model failed to pick the expected reuse rung — how often it would have reinvented or over-built with nothing stopping it. **Delta** is the number of additional cases the gate-enabled run got right versus baseline. Higher reinvention rate is worse; higher delta means the gate helped more.

## Ranking

No benchmark runs recorded yet — run `npm run benchmark` across the models you care about to produce `benchmarks/results/*.json`, then `npm run index` to regenerate this table.

This page reports only measurements from real benchmark runs. Until result files exist it stays in this empty state rather than showing placeholder scores.

## Reproducibility

1. Run the benchmark for each model: `npm run benchmark` (writes `benchmarks/results/<model>.json`).
2. Regenerate this document: `npm run index` (optionally `--as-of <YYYY-MM-DD>`).
3. Every number above is recomputed from the committed result files — none are entered by hand.

Scoring is defined in `scripts/wheel-index.js`; the cases live in `benchmarks/behavior-cases.json`. See `benchmarks/README.md` for the run protocol.
